title: Psalms Chapter 35 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 35 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 35 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 35.

questions.question: In Psalms 35, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Take hold of shield and buckler
Let them be confounded and put to shame
For without cause have they hid for me their net
questions.explanation: The first event in the chapter is the plea to the LORD for help, as stated in Psalms 35:1.

questions.question: What does David ask the LORD to do with those that strive with him?
questions.explanation: David asks the LORD to fight against those who fight against him in Psalms 35:1.

questions.question: What does David ask the LORD to take hold of for his help?
questions.explanation: David specifically asks the LORD to take hold of shield and buckler for his help in Psalms 35:2.

questions.question: What does David request to be drawn out against those who persecute him?
questions.explanation: David requests for the spear to be drawn out against those that persecute him in Psalms 35:3.

questions.question: What does David want to happen to those who seek after his soul?
questions.explanation: David desires that those who seek after his soul be confounded and put to shame as stated in Psalms 35:4.

questions.question: How does David describe the fate of his adversaries?
questions.explanation: David wishes that his adversaries be like chaff before the wind in Psalms 35:5.

questions.question: What does David want the way of his enemies to be?
questions.explanation: David desires that the way of his enemies be dark and slippery in Psalms 35:6.

questions.question: What have David’s enemies hidden for him?
questions.explanation: David states that his enemies have hidden a net in a pit for him in Psalms 35:7.

questions.question: What does David say will happen to the one who has hidden a net for him?
questions.explanation: David asks that destruction come upon the one who has hidden a net for him in Psalms 35:8.

questions.question: What will David’s soul do in the LORD?
questions.explanation: David expresses that his soul shall rejoice in the LORD's salvation in Psalms 35:9.

questions.question: What do all of David's bones say about the LORD?
questions.explanation: David's bones proclaim that the LORD deliverest the poor from those too strong for them in Psalms 35:10.

questions.question: David pleads with the LORD to fight against those who fight against him.
questions.explanation: This is a direct request made by David in Psalms 35:1.

questions.question: David asks the LORD to stand up for him.
questions.explanation: David specifically asks the LORD to stand up for his help in Psalms 35:2.

questions.question: David desires that his enemies be like mountains.
questions.explanation: David desires that his enemies be like chaff before the wind, not mountains, as stated in Psalms 35:5.

questions.question: David's soul will be sorrowful in the LORD.
questions.explanation: David's soul will rejoice in the LORD, not be sorrowful, as stated in Psalms 35:9.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 35 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 35 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did false witnesses do according to Psalms 35:11?
options: They laid to my charge things that I knew not
questions.correctAnswer: They laid to my charge things that I knew not
questions.explanation: This is correct as Psalms 35:11 states that false witnesses rose up and laid charges against David that he was unaware of.

questions.question: What does Psalms 35:12 promise will happen if someone does what verse 11 describes?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 35:12, it follows that the false witnesses rewarded David evil for good, indicating a promise of retribution for wrongdoing.

questions.question: How did David respond when his enemies were sick according to Psalms 35:13?
options: He humbled his soul with fasting
questions.correctAnswer: He humbled his soul with fasting
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:13 indicates that David humbled himself and prayed for them, showing compassion despite their actions.

questions.question: What does Psalms 35:14 reveal about David's feelings towards those who were his enemies?
options: He behaved as though he had been their friend
questions.correctAnswer: He behaved as though he had been their friend
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:14 shows David's empathy and how he mourned for them, indicating his integrity and compassion.

questions.question: What did David observe in Psalms 35:15 regarding those who opposed him?
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:15 describes how his adversaries gathered against him and took pleasure in his suffering.

questions.question: What action do the hypocritical mockers take in Psalms 35:16?
options: They gnashed upon him with their teeth
questions.correctAnswer: They gnashed upon him with their teeth
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:16 depicts the mockers as fiercely attacking David, showing their contempt and hostility.

questions.question: What does David ask the Lord in Psalms 35:17?
options: How long will you bless me?
How long wilt thou look on?
How long will you forsake me?
How long will you punish me?
questions.correctAnswer: How long wilt thou look on?
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:17 reveals David's plea for God to intervene and rescue him from his enemies' destruction.

questions.question: In Psalms 35:18, what does David vow to do when he is rescued?
options: He will give thanks in the great congregation
questions.correctAnswer: He will give thanks in the great congregation
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:18 shows David's commitment to publicly praise God for His deliverance.

questions.question: What warning does Psalms 35:19 give regarding enemies?
options: Let not them that are mine enemies wrongfully rejoice over me
questions.correctAnswer: Let not them that are mine enemies wrongfully rejoice over me
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:19 expresses David's concern about his enemies taking joy in his struggles, emphasizing the desire for justice.

questions.question: What do the enemies devise according to Psalms 35:20?
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:20 indicates that the enemies plot against the peaceful, revealing their treachery and malice.

questions.question: According to Psalms 35:7, why did David's enemies dig a pit for him?
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:7 states that without cause, they laid a trap for David, emphasizing the unjust nature of his plight.

questions.question: In Psalms 35:10, what do David's bones declare about God?
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:10 expresses David's awe at God's unparalleled ability to deliver the needy from their oppressors.

questions.question: Is it true that David prayed for his enemies according to Psalms 35:13?
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:13 shows that David prayed for his enemies when they were sick, demonstrating his compassion.

questions.question: Is it true that David rejoiced when his adversaries faced difficulties according to Psalms 35:15?
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:15 indicates that his adversaries rejoiced in his adversity, not the other way around.

questions.question: Is it true that David's enemies sought peace according to Psalms 35:20?
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:20 clearly states that they do not speak peace but devise deceitful matters against the quiet.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 35 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 35.

questions.question: What did the enemies say against David in Psalms 35:21?
options: Aha, aha, our eye hath seen it.
questions.correctAnswer: Aha, aha, our eye hath seen it.
questions.explanation: This is directly quoted in Psalms 35:21, where the enemies mockingly declare their perceived victory over David.

questions.question: In Psalms 35:22, what does David ask the Lord not to do?
questions.explanation: David pleads with the Lord not to remain silent in the face of his troubles as stated in Psalms 35:22.

questions.question: What does David request in Psalms 35:23?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 35:23, David asks God to stir up Himself and be active in judging his situation.

questions.question: According to Psalms 35:24, how does David want to be judged?
questions.explanation: David requests to be judged by the Lord's righteousness in Psalms 35:24.

questions.question: In Psalms 35:26, what does David wish for those who rejoice at his hurt?
questions.explanation: David desires that those who take joy in his suffering be clothed with shame, as stated in Psalms 35:26.

questions.question: What does David want those who favor his righteous cause to do, according to Psalms 35:27?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 35:27, David encourages those who support him to express joy and magnify the Lord.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'judgment' (mishpat) in Psalms 35:23 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'mishpat' refers to justice, which is the essence of what David seeks in his plea for judgment.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Psalms 35:27 with the phrase 'Let the LORD be magnified'?
questions.explanation: The phrase demonstrates parallelism, a common poetic device in Hebrew literature, reinforcing the idea of glorifying God.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects with the theme of seeking justice as seen in Psalms 35:24?
questions.explanation: Micah 6:8 emphasizes the importance of acting justly, which resonates with David's plea for divine judgment in Psalms 35:24.

questions.question: Which other passage reflects the theme of enemies rejoicing in adversity, similar to Psalms 35:19?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 24:17 warns against rejoicing when one's enemy falls, echoing the sentiment of David in Psalms 35:19.

questions.question: What follows after the plea in Psalms 35:28?
options: And my soul shall be joyful.
Let them be clothed with shame.
questions.correctAnswer: And my soul shall be joyful.
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:28 is followed by the declaration of joy in the Lord, highlighting David's faith despite his struggles.

questions.question: In Psalms 35:15, what was David's experience while facing adversity?
options: He mourned as for a brother.
questions.correctAnswer: He mourned as for a brother.
questions.explanation: David describes his deep sorrow for those who turned against him, paralleling the grief of losing a loved one, as stated in Psalms 35:14.

questions.question: According to Psalms 35:11, what did false witnesses do to David?
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:11 indicates that false witnesses arose against David and accused him of things he did not do.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 35:26 expresses a desire for shame upon those who rejoice at David's hurt.
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:26 indeed expresses David's desire for those who rejoice in his suffering to be ashamed.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 35:22 shows David expressing confidence in God's silence.
questions.explanation: In Psalms 35:22, David is pleading with God not to keep silent, indicating a lack of confidence in God's silence.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 35 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 35 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 35:3 teach about God's role in salvation and spiritual warfare?
options: God is the salvation of the soul and actively intervenes in protecting His people
God passively observes human conflict without intervention
Salvation is achieved solely through human effort without divine aid
God only saves in the afterlife, not in present conflicts
questions.correctAnswer: God is the salvation of the soul and actively intervenes in protecting His people
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:3 states, 'say unto my soul, I am thy salvation,' indicating God's active role as Savior and protector in spiritual conflicts

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 35:10 teach about God's justice towards the poor and needy?
options: God delivers the poor and needy from oppressors who are too strong for them
God ignores the plight of the poor and needy in this life
Salvation is only for the righteous wealthy
God punishes the poor for their suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God delivers the poor and needy from oppressors who are too strong for them
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:10 highlights God's justice by declaring, 'which deliverest the poor from him that is too strong for him,' affirming divine intervention on behalf of the oppressed

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin and false accusation is taught in Psalms 35:11?
options: False witnesses arise to accuse the innocent without cause
All accusations are true and just
Sinful acts are always visible and undeniable
God condones false accusations as a test of faith
questions.correctAnswer: False witnesses arise to accuse the innocent without cause
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:11 states, 'False witnesses did rise up; they laid to my charge things that I knew not,' teaching that human sin includes deceitful accusations against the innocent

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 35:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:5 shows God's sovereign power as 'the angel of the LORD chase them,' demonstrating His authority over enemies

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 35:22 specifically demonstrate?
options: God’s attentiveness and nearness to His people
questions.correctAnswer: God’s attentiveness and nearness to His people
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:22 pleads, 'This thou hast seen, O LORD: keep not silence: O Lord, be not far from me,' showing God’s attentive care and nearness

questions.question: How does Psalms 35 prepare for the New Testament theme of Christ as the righteous sufferer?
options: It anticipates the innocent suffering inflicted by enemies and the plea for divine vindication
It describes the Messiah as a conquering warrior only
It denies that suffering can be redemptive
It focuses solely on Israel’s national enemies without messianic significance
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the innocent suffering inflicted by enemies and the plea for divine vindication
questions.explanation: The psalm's lament over false accusations and unjust suffering (e.g., Psalms 35:11-15) prefigures Christ’s innocent suffering and appeal to the Father for justice (cf. 1 Peter 2:21-23)

questions.question: In what way does Psalms 35:1-3 connect to the theme of divine warfare found in the Old Testament?
options: It portrays God as a warrior fighting on behalf of His people
It depicts God as reluctant to fight for His people
It denies God's involvement in human conflicts
It encourages human revenge without divine help
questions.correctAnswer: It portrays God as a warrior fighting on behalf of His people
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:1-3 uses military imagery ('fight against them that fight against me,' 'shield and buckler'), illustrating God’s role as divine warrior protecting His people, consistent with Old Testament theophanies

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Psalms 35:13 and Psalms 35:14 teach about sanctification and compassion toward enemies?
options: The believer is called to humble self-denial and to treat enemies with brotherly love
The believer should seek revenge and harden their heart
Sanctification requires withdrawing from all social interactions
Compassion is only for friends, not enemies
questions.correctAnswer: The believer is called to humble self-denial and to treat enemies with brotherly love
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:13-14 describes humbling the soul by fasting and behaving toward enemies as friends or brothers, teaching sanctification involves humility and love for adversaries

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 35:18 and Psalms 35:28 teach about worship and testimony?
options: Public praise and continual testimony to God's righteousness are proper responses to deliverance
Worship should be private and silent only
Testifying of God’s righteousness is optional
Praise is only appropriate in times of prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: Public praise and continual testimony to God's righteousness are proper responses to deliverance
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:18 expresses praise in 'the great congregation,' and 35:28 commits the tongue to speak of God's righteousness 'all the day long,' emphasizing public and continual worship

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 35:4 and Psalms 35:26 teach about divine justice and the fate of the wicked?
options: The wicked who devise harm will be confounded, ashamed, and dishonored
The wicked will ultimately prosper without consequence
God is indifferent to the plans of evildoers
The punishment of the wicked is delayed indefinitely
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked who devise harm will be confounded, ashamed, and dishonored
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:4 calls for those who seek harm to be 'confounded and put to shame,' and 35:26 asks that such rejoicers in the Psalmist's hurt be 'clothed with shame and dishonour,' affirming divine justice

questions.question: Sceptics claim Psalms 35:19-21 shows God endorsing deceit and malice among the wicked. What does Psalms 35:19-21 actually teach?
options: The passage condemns deceitful plotting by enemies and calls for God's justice
It praises deceitful enemies as models of faith
It suggests God is silent and indifferent to wickedness
It encourages believers to practice deceit as well
questions.correctAnswer: The passage condemns deceitful plotting by enemies and calls for God's justice
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:19-21 recounts enemies who 'devise deceitful matters' and mock, and the Psalmist's plea for God not to allow them to rejoice, highlighting condemnation of evil, not endorsement

questions.question: What doctrine about prayer and divine response is taught in Psalms 35:23-24?
options: God is to be stirred and awakened to enact righteous judgment for His people
Prayer is ineffective and God remains passive
God is distant and unresponsive to human pleas
Divine judgment is arbitrary and unjust
questions.correctAnswer: God is to be stirred and awakened to enact righteous judgment for His people
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:23-24 calls on God to 'Stir up thyself, and awake' and to 'Judge me according to thy righteousness,' teaching that God actively responds to prayer with just action

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Psalms 35:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:17 pleads, 'rescue my soul from their destructions, my darling from the lions,' highlighting God’s protective deliverance

questions.question: What doctrine about human response to persecution is taught in Psalms 35:12?
options: Believers may be repaid evil for good, reflecting the reality of suffering in a fallen world
Believers always receive good in return for good
Suffering is always a sign of divine punishment
Persecutors act righteously when they harm the godly
questions.correctAnswer: Believers may be repaid evil for good, reflecting the reality of suffering in a fallen world
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:12 says, 'They rewarded me evil for good,' teaching that godly people can suffer unjustly and be treated wickedly, consistent with biblical teaching on persecution

questions.question: How does Psalms 35:27 connect to the broader biblical theme of divine pleasure in the prosperity of His servants?
options: God delights in the prosperity and vindication of His righteous servants
God is indifferent to the prosperity of His people
Prosperity is always a sign of human pride
questions.correctAnswer: God delights in the prosperity and vindication of His righteous servants
questions.explanation: Psalms 35:27 encourages rejoicing for those who favor the Psalmist's cause and declares, 'Let the LORD be magnified, which hath pleasure in the prosperity of his servant,' affirming divine pleasure in blessing the righteous
